images.title: Naming chikki pieces
images.purpose: Set up the question: name each chikki piece by counting the squares it covers and how many such pieces fill the 24 square chikki.
images.composition: The whole chikki grid on the left, and two sample pieces on the right with wide space between them, and one question line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one chikki drawn as a grid of 24 equal small squares, 6 across and 4 down, plain. Right top: piece (a), a rectangle 1 square across and 2 down, filled teal #0072B2, with its grid lines. Right bottom: piece (c), a triangle filled amber #E69F00, drawn inside a dashed grey #6B7280 block of 3 across and 2 down, cut corner to corner so it fills half the block. Exactly 1 grid, 2 pieces, 1 dashed block.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any fraction or square count written on either piece, or a triangle that is not exactly half of its dashed block
images.takeaway: Count the squares a piece covers, then ask how many such pieces fill the chikki.
images.description: A plain 6 by 4 chikki grid of 24 squares beside two sample pieces: a teal 1 by 2 rectangle (a) and an amber triangle (c) that fills half of a dashed 3 by 2 block.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the squares the triangle really covers inside its dashed block before naming it.

image_decisions.why: The whole grid beside two sample pieces gives the counting cue without naming any piece.
